The formal Wick check of \eqref{eq:wick6} enumerates connected
loopless degree-three multigraphs: a graph with multiplicities
$m_{ij}$ has weight $(3!)^r/\prod_{i<j}m_{ij}!$ for $r$ tensors.
There are seven labelled connected fourth-order graphs and $640$
sixth-order graphs. Expanding the three pairings in $S$ gives the
same rational coefficients in each of the six sixth-order graph
classes. This checks the tensor identity, rather than a set of
numerical tensor examples.
changes.new:
To check \eqref{eq:wick6}, pair the three indices in each tensor with
indices in other tensors, retaining patterns that link all tensors.
For $r$ tensors, a pattern with $m_{ij}$ pairs between tensors $i,j$
has weight $(3!)^r/\prod_{i<j}m_{ij}!$. There are seven labelled
multiplicity patterns $(m_{ij})$ for four tensors and $640$ for six.
The six-tensor patterns form six classes when patterns differing only
by relabeling the tensors are grouped together. Expanding the three
pairings in $S$ gives the same rational coefficients in every class.
This checks the tensor identity for every tensor.
